name: Turn-based Gladiator Game
concept_focus: Reusable functions and combat state, then classes, status effects, a thinking opponent and balance by simulation

story.title: Sand and Iron
story.client: Lanista Corvo of the Iron Pit
story.hook: Corvo's arena is dying: every fight is the same, and the crowd has stopped coming. He wants a game worth watching, with classes, tactics and opponents that think. And one day, a fighter fit to face the Unbound, the champion who has never been chained.

acts.title: Act I: The Pit
acts.goal: Rules planned first, then one honest duel with defend and a risky strike.

acts.title: Act II: The Run
acts.goal: Rewards and upgrades, opponents with their own style, a difficulty curve and clean new runs.

acts.title: Act III: The Craft of War
acts.goal: Classes, status effects, the crowd's favour and an opponent that weighs every move.

acts.title: Act IV: The Games
acts.goal: A tournament bracket, a balance simulator and a hall of laurels.

boss_lore: The Unbound fights like you, because it learned from watching you. Change, or lose the way you always do.
boss_brief: Bring a finished gladiator.py: classes built from templates, defend and risky actions, status effects with durations, crowd favour, an opponent that chooses by expected value, upgrades across a run, an eight-fighter bracket, a balance simulation across every class matchup, and a saved hall of laurels.

mobs.name: The Rulescribe
mobs.concept: Planning state and turn order in comments
mobs.encounter: Sketch the combat rules and turn order before coding, naming every piece of state a fighter needs, including the secondary stat.
mobs.contract: Corvo will not let you near the sand until the rules are written. Plan the fight before you fight it.

objectives.label: Write the rules
objectives.brief: At the top of gladiator.py, write the rules as comments: the turn order, the actions, and how damage and stamina work.

objectives.label: Name the state
objectives.brief: Create a fighter dictionary with every stat your rules mention, including a secondary stat such as stamina.

objectives.label: Defend the plan
objectives.brief: Explain one rule you changed while planning and the problem it would have caused in code.

mobs.name: The Arena Recruit
mobs.encounter: Get one full duel working from first strike to a fallen fighter.
mobs.contract: A recruit waits on the sand, shaking. Give the two of you one clean duel, start to finish.

objectives.label: Fight the duel
objectives.brief: Loop turns between the player and an opponent until one falls, using one attack function for both.

objectives.label: Narrate it
objectives.brief: Print each action and both fighters' HP and stamina after every turn.

objectives.label: Trace two turns
objectives.brief: Predict both fighters' HP after two turns with fixed numbers, then check.

mobs.name: The Shield Bearer
mobs.encounter: Add a defend or block action and reason about how long its effect should last.
mobs.contract: The Bearer raises a shield and waits. A good defend lasts exactly as long as it should, and not a turn longer.

objectives.label: Add defend
objectives.brief: Add a defend action that halves the next hit and restores some stamina.

objectives.label: Let it wear off
objectives.brief: Clear the defend effect after it absorbs one hit or at the start of the defender's next turn.

objectives.label: Unstick the shield
objectives.brief: Explain the bug where defending once protects you for the rest of the fight, and show your fix.

mobs.name: The Bloodletter
mobs.encounter: Add a stronger but riskier attack and argue when a player should gamble on it.
mobs.contract: The Bloodletter swings wild: double damage when it lands, nothing when it does not. Make the gamble real and knowable.

objectives.label: Add a heavy strike
objectives.brief: Add a heavy strike that costs more stamina, hits harder and can miss.

objectives.label: Compare the strikes
objectives.brief: Compute and print the expected damage of a normal and a heavy strike.

objectives.label: Argue the gamble
objectives.brief: Explain when the heavy strike is worth it, using the numbers your program prints.

mobs.name: The Bookmaker
mobs.encounter: Award coins or XP after a win and let the player pick an upgrade or item before the next fight.
mobs.contract: The Bookmaker pays winners and sells to them in the same breath. Win, collect, choose how to grow.

objectives.label: Pay the winner
objectives.brief: Award coins after a win, more for a faster victory.

objectives.label: Choose an upgrade
objectives.brief: Offer upgrades from a dictionary (more HP, more attack, a potion) with prices, applying the chosen one to the fighter.

objectives.label: Cap the upgrades
objectives.brief: Explain how buying the same upgrade forever could break the game and add a limit.

mobs.name: The Veteran
mobs.encounter: Give opponents different strengths and a simple rule for choosing actions, and explain why it is more than pure chance.
mobs.contract: The Veteran has a style: it defends when hurt and strikes hard when you are tired. Give every opponent a way of thinking.

objectives.label: Give them styles
objectives.brief: Create opponents with different stat spreads and a style name.

objectives.label: Write their rules
objectives.brief: Write choose_action(fighter, enemy) that picks an action from simple rules based on HP and stamina.

objectives.label: Explain the rules
objectives.brief: Explain how a player can learn to read your Veteran, and why that is fairer than pure chance.

mobs.name: The Champion's Guard
mobs.encounter: Make each opponent tougher across the run and test whether the curve stays challenging but beatable.
mobs.contract: The Guard stands between you and the champion, one fighter stronger than the last. Make the climb steep but never a wall.

objectives.label: Scale the opponents
objectives.brief: Make each fight in a run use a stronger opponent from a formula based on the fight number.

objectives.label: Test the curve
objectives.brief: Simulate runs with a simple automatic player and print how often it survives each fight.

objectives.label: Judge the curve
objectives.brief: Explain from your numbers whether the curve is too steep or too flat, and what you changed.

mobs.name: The Fallen Laurel
mobs.encounter: End the run on defeat with a summary and start a new run without carrying over old upgrades or HP.
mobs.contract: Every champion falls eventually. When yours does, carve the run into the laurel and start the next one clean.

objectives.label: Summarise the run
objectives.brief: On defeat, show fights won, coins earned, upgrades taken and the opponent that ended the run.

objectives.label: Start clean
objectives.brief: Start a new run with a fresh fighter, building it from a starting template rather than resetting fields by hand.

objectives.label: Catch the carry-over
objectives.brief: Explain how old upgrades could leak into a new run and show yours cannot.

mobs.name: The Lanista's Ledger
mobs.encounter: Offer warrior, rogue and mage classes with their own stats and actions.
mobs.contract: Corvo's ledger lists every kind of fighter he has trained. Each class plays differently, and all of them are written down as data.

objectives.label: Write the classes
objectives.brief: Define at least three classes in a dictionary with base stats and a signature action each.

objectives.label: Pick a class
objectives.brief: Let the player choose a class at the start of a run and build their fighter from it.

objectives.label: Make them different
objectives.brief: Implement each signature action so the classes really play differently.

mobs.name: The Bleeding Edge
mobs.encounter: Add bleed and stun that last several turns.
mobs.contract: Some wounds keep cutting after the blade is gone. Add effects that last, and make sure something counts them down.

objectives.label: Add bleed and stun
objectives.brief: Let actions apply bleed (damage each turn) and stun (lose a turn), each with turns remaining, stored on the fighter.

objectives.label: Tick the effects
objectives.brief: Apply and count down effects at the start of the affected fighter's turn and remove them when they expire.

objectives.label: Prevent stun locks
objectives.brief: Explain how repeated stuns could stop a fighter ever acting, and add a rule that prevents it.

mobs.name: The Crowd's Roar
mobs.concept: A meter driven by many events
mobs.encounter: Track the crowd's favour and let it change rewards.
mobs.contract: The crowd decides who lives and who gets paid. Daring moves make it roar; turtling makes it boo.

objectives.label: Track favour
objectives.brief: Keep a crowd favour meter from 0 to 100 that rises on heavy strikes and comebacks and falls on repeated defends.

objectives.label: Pay for favour
objectives.brief: Multiply rewards by the crowd's favour and show the meter during fights.

objectives.label: Predict the meter
objectives.brief: Predict the meter after a scripted sequence of actions, then check it.

mobs.name: The Thinking Blade
mobs.encounter: Make an opponent that scores every action and picks the best.
mobs.contract: The deadliest opponent does not follow rules. It asks, for every action: what do I gain, what do I risk? Then it chooses.

objectives.label: Score every action
objectives.brief: Write a function that scores each available action by expected damage dealt, damage avoided and stamina cost.

objectives.label: Choose the best
objectives.brief: Make an opponent that takes the highest-scoring action each turn.

objectives.label: Prove it thinks
objectives.brief: Pit it against your rule-based Veteran over 500 fights and explain the result.

mobs.name: The Bracket Master
mobs.contract: The Games are coming: eight fighters, three rounds, one laurel. The Bracket Master pairs them and nobody gets a bye they did not earn.

objectives.label: Seed the bracket
objectives.brief: Seed eight fighters by strength so the strongest meet last.

objectives.label: Run the rounds
objectives.brief: Pair the winners of each round until one remains, with the player fighting their matches and the others simulated.

objectives.label: Show the bracket
objectives.brief: Print the bracket after each round showing who advanced.

mobs.name: The Balance Oracle
mobs.encounter: Simulate every class matchup to find what is overpowered.
mobs.contract: Corvo hears complaints that rogues always win. The Oracle answers with numbers: every matchup, a thousand times.

objectives.label: Simulate the matchups
objectives.brief: Simulate 1,000 fights for every pair of classes using your thinking opponent on both sides.

objectives.label: Show the table
objectives.brief: Print a win-rate table of every class against every other.

objectives.label: Fix the balance
objectives.brief: Find the most lopsided matchup, change one number, and show the new table to prove it is closer to fair.

mobs.name: The Hall of Laurels
mobs.encounter: Keep the best runs between sessions and give the game a front door.
mobs.contract: Every champion's name goes on the hall's walls. Save the best runs, and let Corvo's visitors choose how they want to fight.

objectives.label: Save the best runs
objectives.brief: Save the top ten runs (class, fights won, coins, crowd favour) to a JSON file, sorted best first.

objectives.label: Show the hall
objectives.brief: Show the hall of laurels on start and highlight a new entry.

objectives.label: Open the gates
objectives.brief: Add a menu: start a run, enter the Games bracket, run the balance oracle, view the hall, or quit.
